property_summary: For any caller and any _accessControl, calling initialize(...) on the correct contract sets Initializable._initialized to 1 (initializer marks contract initialized); the mutant that omits __UUPSUpgradeable_init() leaves the initialized flag different for some inputs (e.g., when construction vs top-level call semantics differ), so the observable initialized version differs between P and M for some fuzzed _accessControl addresses.

For every address _accessControl, calling initialize(_accessControl) on the correct contract always returns (does not revert) and sets the contract to be initialized (initializer succeeds as an external top-level call); the mutant that omits __UUPSUpgradeable_init() can cause initialize(...) to revert (due to Initializable construction-vs-initializer semantics) for some _accessControl values, so the observable success/failure of initialize differs for some inputs.

For any fuzzed admin address, calling initialize(admin) on the correct contract always sets the contract to be non-delegated proxiable (proxiableUUID() callable in non-delegated context) — i.e., proxiableUUID() returns the implementation slot when called directly — while the mutant that skips __UUPSUpgradeable_init() can leave the contract in a context where proxiableUUID() reverts (UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext) for some admin addresses; the test asserts that a direct external call to proxiableUUID() succeeds for every fuzzed admin after initialize(...) completes.

After initialize(_accessControl) completes, calling proxiableUUID() externally on the instance must always revert with UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext when the contract is not the implementation (i.e., when called via a proxy context) — the reference C ensures proxiableUUID() is protected by notDelegated and will revert when called through delegatecall context created by an attacker proxy, whereas the mutant that skipped __UUPSUpgradeable_init() can leave the contract callable without that protection in some delegatecall setups, allowing proxiableUUID() to unexpectedly succeed; the test deploys a simple proxy that delegatecalls initialize and then attempts an external call to proxiableUUID() through the proxy to observe the differing behavior.

For every address _accessControl, calling initialize(_accessControl) as an external top-level call on the correct contract C always leaves the contract in an externally callable (non-reverting) initialized state such that a subsequent external call to proxiableUUID() (called directly on the instance) returns the implementation slot without reverting; the mutant that omits __UUPSUpgradeable_init() can leave initialization state that makes proxiableUUID() revert (UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext) for some _accessControl inputs, so the property (proxiableUUID() returns successfully after initialize) is violated for some fuzz inputs.

After initialize(...) returns successfully, the Initializable initialized version reported by _getInitializedVersion() equals 1 for the correct contract for every input; the mutant sets initialized to 2 during initialization so for some inputs the reported initialized version becomes 2 and thus differs.
